## 4d730bbef8df

**Finding: the production three-demo lesson can teach only one diagonal orientation, then require the unseen orientation in its query.** This is a reproduced lesson/shortcut defect, not a reference-rule disagreement. At seed **11**, start/sample index **0**, default difficulty (`null`), no overrides, the three demonstrations all lack an opposite-slope aligned pair. A rival that draws red cells only between crosses on top-left to bottom-right diagonals (`dr = dc`) agrees exactly with all three authoritative demonstration outputs. The query has an additional top-right to bottom-left connection and the rival misses it.

The production command `generate 4d730bbef8df --count 1 --seed 11 --sample-index 0 --train 3 --test 1 --allow-unapproved` completes successfully, accepts sample indices **0, 1, 2, 3**, and records **zero rejections**. Its four inputs and outputs exactly match the focused probe and supported CLI `apply` receipt. Each input also passes the generator's `self_check` with an empty problem list. The first three rival comparisons have zero differing cells; the query differs at exactly the following zero-based coordinates:

| Cell | Racket | Rival |
|---|---:|---:|
| (5, 11) | 2 | 0 |
| (6, 10) | 2 | 0 |

The query's opposite-slope centers are **(4, 12)** and **(7, 9)**. Its other aligned pair, **(3, 5)** to **(7, 9)**, is correctly connected by the rival. Thus the difference isolates diagonal orientation rather than general connection detection, color choice, or no-op behavior.

The source declares `EXAMPLES_NEEDED = 3` and says three demos cover a mix of diagonal and non-diagonal pairs. That mix does not guarantee evidence for both slopes. The main pair starts in the upper-left region and frequently uses positive row and column steps; opposite-slope connections can arise from independently sampled decoys without a lesson-level coverage constraint. A learner can therefore follow a consistent, natural one-orientation interpretation of the demonstrations and fail the emitted query. A targeted follow-up would require both orientations in the visible lesson whenever either can occur in the query, or explicitly test such a rival during lesson assembly. No source fix is proposed in this findings-only audit.

**Evidence and binding.** `checks/audit/4d730bbef8df/probe.py` reproduces the bounded search and retains the rival. `input.json`, `rival.json`, `racket.json`, `episode.jsonl`, and `comparison.json` retain all four grids, production acceptance, authoritative outputs, and the exact cell diff. `commands.json` records working directories, argv, environment, exit codes and WORK-relative evidence paths. `source-hashes.json` binds generator SHA-256 **d44ad9f73a75d39fd0adac6c345719bf6b2cbd60efb60703a377b9154a13b2b8** and exact canonical program text SHA-256 **a60419d75cced06648d8e15c97574a999281bcbe3d9b2bfe0e0478418976ec3f**. The executed callable text has SHA-256 **5ca8db2b872b345af0bba6811eb87d7774d8e12bedffccfd2f2a606d4126943f**, as recorded in `comparison.json` and `racket.json`; these are different text representations of the bound rule. `racket.json` reports executed rule hash **ac716c8f961e**, matching the catalog, with four valid outputs and no errors. The canonical rule is retained in `reference-rule.json`.

**Measured scope and limits.** Inspected the assigned generator, summary, current notes/evidence and canonical rule/pairs. The deterministic search examined default seeds **0–11**, four sample indices per seed (**48 generated inputs**), then stopped at the first structural candidate. Only the four witness inputs were labelled with CLI `apply`; one production episode confirmed their actual admission. This establishes the retained witness, not a library-wide failure rate or exhaustiveness. Other axes, difficulty bands, rotations, and full batteries were not exercised. The catalog receipt already labels this task `unsafe`/unapproved; this finding does not assert a new approval regression.

## 4d730bbef8df

**Reproduced teaching defect — one diagonal orientation is unidentifiable in a
production three-demo lesson.** The current audited generator SHA-256 is
`d44ad9f73a75d39fd0adac6c345719bf6b2cbd60efb60703a377b9154a13b2b8`;
it is unchanged from the existing unresolved audit record.

At seed `11`, default difficulty, no overrides, and sample indices `0,1,2,3`, the
supported production command emitted three demonstrations and one query with no
rejections. A natural rival connects plus centers only on NW-SE diagonals
(`dr = dc`). It matches all three authoritative demonstration outputs exactly.
The query also contains an opposite-slope pair, centers `(4,12)` and `(7,9)`, so
the rival misses the canonical color-2 connector cells `(5,11)` and `(6,10)`.
All four outputs are from the canonical Racket rule; executed rule hash
`ac716c8f961e`, program UTF-8 SHA-256
`a60419d75cced06648d8e15c97574a999281bcbe3d9b2bfe0e0478418976ec3f`.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/4d730bbef8df/episode.jsonl` — exact admitted production episode,
  inputs, Racket outputs, provenance, and no rejections.
- `checks/audit/4d730bbef8df/reproduce.py` — bounded one-slope rival replay.
- `checks/audit/4d730bbef8df/comparison.json` — three demo matches and exact two-cell
  query difference, bound to the current generator hash.
- `checks/audit/4d730bbef8df/generate.log` — command result.

This establishes one source-bound witness, not a failure rate. The generator is
already catalogued unapproved/unsafe and declares no lesson hook or rivals. No
audit-target source was changed. A repair should require both diagonal slopes in
the visible demonstrations whenever the query can require either, or declare and
check the one-slope rival during episode assembly.

triage.reason: Both source-bound audit reports retained and explicitly unresolved within their recorded scopes. This does not clear older findings or upgrade audited generators.
